WF-02, step 1b (second gate pass of at most three) — check again the design docs/design/REQ-104-e2e-chrome-kit.md after the rework 01c (handoffs/E2E104-20261103-01/step-01c-code-designer.json) by the same section "Step 1b" of docs/workflows/WF-02-development.md and by your own first-pass remarks in handoffs/E2E104-20261103-01/step-01b-code-design-validator.json. Read the design itself.
Check in particular: (1) F1, F2, F3 (blocking in the first pass) are really closed — REPEAT yourself the measurements behind the new rules on a fresh clone of the tag base/E2E104-20261103-01 outside the project (NODE_TEST_CONTEXT cleared in the spec environment gives a TAP with `# tests`; the spec path form `test/e2e/<name>.e2e.js` relative to tools/ is the string node prints; the criterion-11 grep and E2K-50 against the design's test list: build the grep tokens from criterion 11 of REQ-104 and search the described test texts and fixtures paths); (2) the F4 answer (process group, SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 5 s on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP and on the 120 s timeout): is it complete, is the signal hook safe (no handler leaks, no double kill, exit codes), is the added code size sensible for this requirement or is it work beyond the criteria (the designer offers dropping E2K-38, M59, M60, row 17 and the signal hook as a smaller alternative — judge it); (3) nothing new broke: the replacement table still fixes exactly HC-02, HC-03, HO-54, PK-7b, LP-3, CTL-13 without weakening; the criterion → test table covers criteria 1-13; the bar section; no implementation code; no contradiction with decisions 0107 and 0108; (4) apply at least 10 mutants again, at least 5 of them from the new M55-M61 and E2K-36/37/38 area, plus several of your own around the rework. Answers of ORCH in decisions/0108 are binding; О7b and REQ-033/REQ-014 are open for the owner and not a reason to FAIL.
MAC LOAD: one agent at a time; at most one full `npm test`; kill every Chrome you start by process id; remove only temp folders you created; never rm inside the project.
Result: PASS or FAIL with a list (section, item, what is wrong).

findings.pass_item: pass C, item 8 (and pass B, item 6)
findings.place: section 11.3, paragraph 'Folder tools/test/fixtures/e2e/tap/ ...' (the capture command and 'failing.txt'); section 10 criterion 11 row; E2K-34
findings.what: The tap texts are captured by 'env -u NODE_TEST_CONTEXT node --test --test-reporter=tap test/fixtures/e2e/specs/<name>.e2e.js > ...'. For 'fail' the TAP holds 'location: ...' and 'stack: ... file:///<absolute path of the capturing machine>/tools/test/fixtures/e2e/specs/fail.e2e.js:3:9' (measured in the clone). On the owner's machines that is a path inside the home folder (Mac) or a drive path (Windows PC): measured with the path replaced by a home-folder-style path, 'npm run traces' (step 3 of 'check') reports 'путь домашнего каталога' for tools/test/fixtures/e2e/tap/failing.txt lines 7 and 12. So following the design literally makes 'check' red and criterion 11 ('npm run -s traces | grep -c -E tools/test/e2e|tools/test/fixtures/e2e' -> 0) unmet; the tester would have to choose by himself how to clean the file (Q6 forbids silencing the rule). The note 'the duration_ms figures ... no test reads them' does not cover the paths.
findings.needed: State how failing.txt (and any text with a location/stack line) is produced so that it holds no path of the capturing machine: say which lines E2K-34 needs from it (the 'not ok' line and the '# tests/# pass/# fail/...' lines) and that the location/stack lines are removed or replaced by a neutral relative text, or that the file is written without the YAML block; and add that the file must pass 'npm run traces' (criterion 11).

findings.place: section 4.4 (addSignalHook, installHandlers), section 6 flow steps 1, 4, 5 and the paragraph 'Exit codes', section 8 row 'Clean-up', section 7 row 17
findings.what: The signal hook is sound as measured (see summary), but five points are left to the developer: (a) the hook is returned as 'remove' by addSignalHook, yet nothing says the runner calls it when the run ends; E2K-32 runs runAll six times in one test process, so six stale hooks would stay and run on a later signal; (b) the hook is 'installed before the first spec starts', but the record line and INTERRUPTED are said to be printed 'in all cases'; a signal during listSpecs or the preflight (up to 20 s) has no hook, so the process exits 143 with neither INTERRUPTED nor the record line; (c) the stop of the hook must unregister the spec group (otherwise cleanupAllSync sends a second SIGKILL to a pgid that may be gone); (d) what happens when a hook throws (the handler is async: an unhandled rejection before cleanupAllSync); the value of 'its own limit' of a hook is not given (only the 10 s total); (e) the exit code after a second signal is not stated.
findings.needed: One sentence each: the runner removes its hook in a finally; the hook is installed together with installHandlers (step 1) and the INTERRUPTED/record output is made for a signal at any moment of runAll, or the preflight window is named as the exception; stop() unregisters the group; a hook error is caught and the clean-up still runs; the exit code after a second signal.

findings.place: section 6 signature 'spawnSpec({ args, cwd, env }) -> child' and E2K-37 ('the record says the process is detached'); section 6 step 4 ('launchBrowser()'), E2K-32
findings.what: (a) The injected spawnSpec receives only args, cwd and env, so a recorder cannot see 'detached' (it is inside the default implementation); the E2K-37 assertion cannot be written as worded, and what a fake child must look like (pid, stdout, close) so that registerGroup is not given a foreign pid is not said. (b) Step 4 says the preflight calls launchBrowser() without env, while E2K-32 runs 'with the stand-in for the preflight' and with an injected env; it is not said that the preflight uses the injected 'launch' option (with the runner's env), so a developer may launch the real Chrome from E2K-32.
findings.needed: (a) Add 'detached: true' to the argument that spawnSpec receives (or move the assertion to E2K-33/E2K-38) and say what the injected fake returns. (b) Say that the preflight calls the option 'launch' with the runner's env, and that E2K-32 injects a launch that starts the stand-in.

result.judgement_f4_size: Keep the hook. The 120 s watchdog (binding by 0108 O3) needs the spec in its own process group (a SIGKILL of the leader alone leaves the file child, repeated by me), and a detached group no longer receives the terminal's Ctrl-C, so without the hook an interrupted 'npm run check' leaves the spec and its Chrome running until the file ends. The extra over the watchdog is small: addSignalHook (about the size of one function), the INTERRUPTED code, one test (E2K-38), one fixture (sleep-chrome), M59/M60, row 17. Dropping E2K-38, M59, M60, row 17 and the hook would be a smaller design but a worse command; I do not require it.
